chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ...
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** The bringing-forth of truth as it proceeds from interior wisdom and is perceived by the [GAP-1: REVIEW — faculties of perception]. [GAP-2: — what is implied is the hidden origin of truth in the will before it is articulated] The initial affection of the will elevates it from within, and the understanding unfolds and explicates it, and the natural-rational faculty distinguishes it into particulars, and the outermost faculty of expression gathers and contains it. Thus truth proceeds into communicable form through the complete series of these five faculties and becomes perceptible beyond the one in whom it originates.

**¶2:** In like manner, a doctrine of truth prepared for use among souls: One operation brings the raw substance of perception into initial form, and another works and shapes it through repeated acts of understanding, and another refines it by removing what is extraneous and false, and another authenticates it with the seal of good so that it bears the mark of its origin, and another purifies it through final discrimination. [GAP-3: REVIEW — "See, then, that"] these five interior operations shape and perfect [GAP-4: REVIEW — their] doctrine of truth, and it enters into the spiritual community. It becomes a good that can be received into the understanding and communicated to others through charity.

**¶3:** So it is also with truth proceeding from wisdom: it is formed and perfected through the complete series of five faculties. It goes forth from interior states and is perceived by the [GAP-5: REVIEW — faculties of perception in] others.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: the production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. [For the chest brings it forth] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.

Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.
This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "faculties of perception," and in the natural-plane vocabulary of the Kephalaia, the ears are the organs by which a spoken word is perceived — confirmed by ¶3 which repeats "heard by the ears."

fills.fill: For the chest brings it forth
fills.explanation: The text explicitly says "these five members" but only four (throat, tongue, teeth, lips) are listed after the gap; the spiritual reading identifies the gap as "the hidden origin of truth in the will before it is articulated," which in the natural register of speech corresponds to the chest/lungs producing the initial breath — the most interior of the five speech organs.

The spiritual reading gives "See, then, that" and "Behold" is the standard Kephalaia demonstrative particle introducing a summarizing observation, fitting perfectly here to present the conclusion of the coin analogy.
The spiritual reading confirms "their" — the possessive refers to the five craftsmen and their coin, the doctrine of truth they collectively shaped through five successive operations.

The spiritual reading confirms "faculties of perception in others," and the natural-plane construction "the ears of others" requires the preposition "of" to connect the organ of perception to those who perceive.
